note.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases. By volume, it is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen; the remaining small proportion includes carbon dioxide, noble gases and variable water vapour.
examples: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in air.
Water vapour in air varies with humidity.
note.simple: Air is not one gas. It is a mixture, and most of it is nitrogen.
note.checkQuestion: Which gas makes up the largest proportion of air, and what is its approximate percentage?
note.title: Composition of the Atmosphere
steps: Read the gas name in the table.
Match it with its percentage by volume.
Remember that water vapour is variable, depending on humidity.
note.answer: Clean, dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with the remainder made up of noble gases and carbon dioxide.

mcqs.stem: Which gas forms the largest part of the atmosphere by volume?
rationales: Correct: nitrogen makes up about 78% of air, more than any other gas.
Incorrect: oxygen makes up about 21% of air.
Incorrect: carbon dioxide is a minor constituent, about 0.04% in the table.
Incorrect: the amount of water vapour varies with humidity.

mcqs.stem: What percentage of air is nitrogen, approximately?
rationales: Incorrect: about 21% of air is oxygen.
Correct: nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of air.
Incorrect: the table gives about 0.04% for carbon dioxide.
Incorrect: the table gives about 1% for noble gases.

mcqs.stem: Which gas makes up about 21% of the atmosphere?
rationales: Correct: oxygen makes up about 21% of air.
Incorrect: nitrogen makes up about 78% of air.
Incorrect: argon is listed as 0.934%.
Incorrect: carbon dioxide is listed as 0.04%.

options: It is always exactly the same.
It is variable depending on humidity.
It is absent from the atmosphere.
mcqs.stem: How does the amount of water vapour in air vary?
rationales: Incorrect: the table says its amount is variable.
Correct: water vapour varies depending on humidity.
Incorrect: about 78% of air is nitrogen.
Incorrect: water vapour is a constituent of the atmosphere.

mcqs.stem: Which branch of chemistry studies chemicals and other pollutants in the environment and their adverse effects?
rationales: Correct: this is the definition of environmental chemistry given in the section.
Incorrect: organic chemistry mainly studies carbon compounds.
Incorrect: physical chemistry studies the physical principles and behaviour of chemical systems.
Incorrect: analytical chemistry deals with identifying and measuring substances.

options: A blanket of air made up of several layers of gases
A single layer of pure oxygen
A mixture made only of nitrogen and oxygen
A layer of water vapour around Earth
mcqs.stem: Which description best matches the atmosphere?
rationales: Correct: the section describes the atmosphere as a blanket of air made up of several layers of gases.
Incorrect: the atmosphere contains several gases, not pure oxygen.
Incorrect: air also contains minor constituents such as carbon dioxide and noble gases.
Incorrect: the atmosphere is made up of several gases, not only water vapour.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask for the approximate composition of clean, dry air. Learn nitrogen as 78% and oxygen as 21%.
A table-reading question may ask for the percentage of a minor constituent. Read the table carefully: carbon dioxide is 0.04% and argon is 0.934%.
For a question about water vapour, write that its amount is variable and depends on humidity.
For a definition question, write the full idea: environmental chemistry studies chemicals and pollutants in the environment and their adverse effects.

explain.title: Environmental chemistry
explain.body: The branch of Chemistry which deals with the study of chemicals and other pollutants in the environment is called environmental chemistry. It also covers the adverse effects of these chemicals on living and non-living things.

explain.title: The atmosphere
explain.body: Earth is covered with a blanket of air called the “atmosphere” which is made up of several layers of gases. Air is essential for life on Earth, for animals to breathe and for plants to make their food.

explain.title: The main gases in air
explain.body: Air contains more nitrogen than any other gas. The table gives nitrogen as 78.0% and oxygen as 21.0% by volume.

explain.title: Minor constituents
explain.body: The table gives carbon dioxide as 0.04% and argon as 0.934%. It lists noble gases as about 1.0%. Water vapour is variable depending upon the humidity.

mistakes: Do not reverse the percentages: nitrogen is about 78%, while oxygen is about 21%.
Do not say that carbon dioxide makes up 1% of air; the table gives 0.04%.
Do not give water vapour a fixed percentage; its amount is variable depending on humidity.
Do not describe the atmosphere as one gas. It is made up of several gases.
